newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan loan body to refuse Tobishima request - paper.
newsitem.headline: Japan loan body to refuse Tobishima request - paper.

text.p: Japan's Housing Loan Administration Corp (HLAC) has said it would not accept a request by general contractor Tobishima Corp that it and other creditors reduce their claims against it for debts owed by its group companies, a business daily said on Thursday.

The Nihon Keizai Shimbun said HLAC, an institution set up to collect problem loans incurred by failed mortgage firms, currently holds loans worth about 42 billion yen owed by the Tobishima group. The HLAC took over the debts from financial institutions.
HLAC officials were not immediately available for comment.

Debt-ridden Tobishima announced last week that it had drawn up a new restructuring plan to try to solve its financial difficulties. It said it would ask its creditors to reduce their claims against it for debts owed by its group companies to 100 billion yen from about 740 billion yen.
Tobishima has said it has fallen into financial difficulties due to lending for property-related business.

Fuji Bank Ltd, one of Tobishima's major creditors, said on Monday it plans to set aside loan loss reserves against its loans to Tobishima in its earnings for the year to next March 31. It did not specify the size of the planned move.
